Misinformation spreads fast online—emotional or surprising posts get attention before anyone checks if they're true, and algorithms reinforce whatever people already click on. This video covers a quick process for evaluating claims: who made it, what evidence backs it up, and what other reliable sources say. It also covers habits like reading past the headline, checking for missing context, and watching for posts designed to provoke anger or fear.

State and local governments make many of the decisions that shape daily life—schools, roads, parks, libraries, policing, elections, and local budgets. This video breaks down how state government splits into legislative, executive, and judicial branches, and how local government can include city, county, school district, and tribal institutions. It also covers how to figure out who actually has power over an issue you care about, and how to get involved before you're even old enough to vote.

Trust in government isn't blind faith. It's the belief that public institutions are basically fair, lawful, and accountable—the thing that makes democracy function at all: voting, following laws, accepting election results, working together on public problems. Healthy distrust demands evidence and works through democratic channels; destructive cynicism assumes government is always corrupt and leads people to check out. Trust gets built when governments are transparent and accountable, and when citizens stay informed and engaged.
